text:
maya: Heads up — during last night's RBAC migration we noticed a handful of Vault wrapped ciphertexts leaked into an internal S3 lifecycle export. Not public internet, but accessible to a handful of partner accounts. filing initial triage here.
aj: ack. timeline? how many objects and which bucket?
sam: saw ~12 objects in s3://redwood-infra-logs/iam-exports/2023-11-07 that include base64 ciphertext blobs and a small header referencing transit:key=wrapping-key-v1
maya: exact header snippet: `wrapped: true; backend=transit; key=wrapping-key-v1; nonce=...` — looks like a wrap key id rather than plaintext creds.
leo: if it's transit-wrapped ciphertext, compromise surface depends on whether wrapping key or wrapped ciphertexts were leaked. do we know KMS permissions on wrapping-key-v1?
aj: wrapping-key-v1 is a GCP KMS key with very limited IAM (only vault-service-account and ops-kms-rotor). no external access keys. but partner accounts could have read access to that S3 prefix due to a temporary ACL during migration.
security-bot: automated alert: vault-audit-logs show export job id export-20231107 created by terraform-runner at 03:12UTC. Audit entries reference: sys/wrapping/unwrap? none recorded.
maya: good — no unwrap recorded. that reduces risk but we should still treat as sensitive because if any partner ever gets KMS access or SA key leaked, they could unwrap.
sam: immediate steps proposed: 1) revoke all leases for affected paths 2) rotate the transit wrapping key (rekey/roll new primary) 3) rewrap ciphertext blobs in our backups with new wrapping key 4) tighten S3 prefix ACLs and revoke partner access 5) add audit hooks and alert rules for any unwrap attempts
leo: agree. also add a short TTL on the rewrapped ciphertext to limit long-term use. can we rewrap in-place for those S3 objects?
aj: yes, but rewrap requires the plaintext or a transit rewrap API. Hashicorp Vault has `transit/rewrap` which rewraps without exposing plaintext if you have access to both old and new key versions. we'll script a job that reads objects, calls Vault rewrap, writes back.
maya: ops-oncall can we schedule a low-risk window for rewrap job? want to ensure we don't accidentally change production secrets.
ops-oncall: available at 2200UTC. prefer read-only dry-run first. will run under ops-rotation role. will isolate to a staging copy of the bucket before writing back.
sam: checklist for the operation (short): - create staging copy of the 12 objects - rotate/roll transit key: create new key version in GCP KMS + update Vault transit key config to use new wrap key as primary - run `vault write transit/rewrap` job against staging objects - validate rewrapped blobs by calling Vault unwrap in staging with ops-rotor creds (no persistence) - copy back to production prefix and tighten ACLs
aj: note: we must also update Terraform state PR that temporarily granted s3:GetObject to partner-account principal. revert that PR and run `terraform apply` ASAP.
maya: legal/partners: need a short disclosure note. nobody accessed unwrap, but we should notify partner security that objects were accidentally readable for ~90 minutes. Sam, can you draft? keep it minimal and technical.
sam: I can. propose: what happened, what we found, actions taken (revoked ACL, rotated key, rewrap, audit logs), contact for followup.
leo: one more item: enable real-time detection rule: if any `sys/wrapping/unwrap` calls appear from non-zero src IPs OR if a new SA is granted `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` for wrapping-key-v1, trigger high-sev pager.
security-bot: created ticket SEC-2023-245 for rotation + audit, assigned to aj + ops-oncall. reminder scheduled in 2h for status update.
aj: small technical detail for the rewrap script: use streaming rewrap to avoid pulling plaintext into disk. pseudo: ```
for obj in list_objects(prefix):
  ciphertext = download(obj)
  new_cipher = vault_cli('transit/rewrap', ciphertext, key=wrapping-key-v2)
  upload(staging_prefix + obj.key, new_cipher)
```
maya: ensure the job runs with a short-lived SA token, not long-lived creds. prefer GCP Workload Identity or short service account key generated by ops-rotor.
ops-oncall: using Workload Identity for the job. will attach least-privilege role: storage.objects.get/list, storage.objects.create for staging prefix, vault transit:rewrap permission via vault policies.
sam: once rewrap done, rotate any service tokens that referenced those objects just in case (low-cost precaution). which services read that prefix historically?
aj: only terraform-runner & backup-inspector. will rotate terraform-runner runner tokens and confirm backup-inspector uses scoped ephemeral creds.
maya: action owners and ETA: - aj: revert Terraform ACL PR (ETA 30m) - ops-oncall: staging copy + dry-run rewrap at 2200UTC (ETA run time) - sam: partner disclosure draft in 60m - leo: add detection rule & alert (ETA 4h) - maya: coordinate legal + incident summary (ETA 2h)
leo: quick question: do we need to call GCP KMS rotate (create new key version) or create an entirely new key? my vote: create new key version and set IAM bindings identically, then update Vault mapping to new key version. avoids re-provisioning permissions.
aj: agreed. create new key version is fine; Vault transit config needs to be told to use new encryption key id. we should also rewrap with a different key name (wrapping-key-v2) to be extra safe and then deprecate v1.
ops-oncall: during dry-run we will assert unwrap fails against v1 after rotation and succeeds for v2 for staging objects.
sam: disclosure draft ready — posting to #partners-security for review and then send to the partner list. pinging @legal for a quick read.
maya: once all steps are validated, we'll close SEC-2023-245 and update runbook with a short note: "during RBAC migration a temporary S3 ACL exposed wrapped Vault ciphertexts; no unwrap activity observed; rewrap and key rotation completed; tightened ACLs and added detection".
aj: small followup: also scrub S3 access logs to confirm which principals accessed the prefix during the window. if partner principal didn't actually GET objects, that is even better.
leo: schedule a 30m postmortem tomorrow morning to review runbook gaps and Terraform drift checks.
ops-oncall: starting the staging copy now, will report back after dry-run.
maya: thanks all. keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
